identity.title: On Linear Mode Connectivity of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures

problem.claim: Investigate whether and how Linear Mode Connectivity (LMC) occurs in Mixture-of-Experts architectures.

gap.claim: Prior LMC studies focused on standard neural networks, leaving its behavior in MoE architectures to be systematically examined.

contributions.claim: Characterizes MoE symmetries as permutations acting on both expert components and the gating function, covering dense and sparse gating.
Proposes a matching algorithm to align independently trained MoEs and facilitate discovery of LMC.
Reports LMC across dense, sparse, and shared-expert MoE variants under varied model settings and datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MoE symmetries are fully characterized by permutations of experts and the gating function.
The authors report empirical LMC across diverse MoE configurations, including dense, sparse, and shared-expert variants.
The authors report that these results provide insights into the functional landscape and optimization dynamics of deep learning models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines LMC as low-loss linear connectivity between independently trained models up to permutation symmetries.
Extends the investigation from standard neural networks to scalable, computationally efficient MoE architectures.
Analyzes dense and sparse gating and identifies the relevant expert and gating-function permutation symmetries.
Uses a proposed alignment algorithm to investigate LMC and reports it across MoE variants, settings, and datasets.
Frames the findings as insights into neural-network loss geometry and optimization dynamics.

source_observation.claim: The abstract first identifies the architecture's permutation symmetries, then uses them to design a matching algorithm for independently trained models.

lessons.interpretation: Explicitly resolving symmetry can turn an abstract connectivity question into a concrete model-alignment procedure.
lessons.application: For another architecture with parameter symmetries, characterize those transformations before defining a matching or connectivity test.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the architecture has no relevant symmetry or when the claimed phenomenon is invariant to alignment.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative loss values, path details, or comparison baselines for the reported LMC.
The matching algorithm, model settings, datasets, and meaning of “fully characterized” are not specified in enough detail to assess scope or reproducibility.
